item.title: Advance Notice: Vanuatu Resilient Education Infrastructure
item.description:
RFx ID: 34134620
Organisation: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade
Open date: Wednesday, 20 May 2026 4:00 PM +12:00
Close date: Friday, 19 February 2027 5:00 PM +13:00
Categories: 72100000 - Building and facility maintenance and repair services
72120000 - Nonresidential building construction services
Region: International
Overview: This is a Notice of Information (Advance Notice) from The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFAT) for provision of construction services on behalf of the Ministry of Education and Training (MoET) in Vanuatu, as part of New Zealand’s International Development Cooperation (IDC) Programme. The goal is to provide resilient, inclusive and sustainable education infrastructure in Vanuatu, as well as responding to the ongoing natural disaster recovery needs.

MFAT is looking to engage a construction contractor to complete works at various school sites in Vanuatu, including the provision of labour, plant, materials, project management services, logistics, etc. to complete construction works under three different workstreams:
1. Clear the backlog of repair and reconstruction from previous natural disasters
2. Repair and reconstruction of facilities damaged in future disasters
3. Support MoET ‘business as usual’ school upgrades programme

The location of works will be dispersed across Vanuatu, therefore the contractor must be prepared to mobilise for works outside of Port Vila. The term for this contract may extend up until 2033 with periodic reviews if the supplier demonstrates their continued ability to respond to the requirements. The estimated contract value over this period would be up to NZD $16.3 million with potential extension subject to approval.

The procurement will be conducted via an open market, two stage tender process including a Registration of Interest (RoI) phase to create a shortlist who will then be invited to submit a response to a Request for Proposal (RFP). We are looking for suppliers who can demonstrate capability and capacity to deliver on time and budget, with relevant Pacific Experience, and ensuring all quality and H&S requirements are met. This is a unique opportunity for suppliers to secure a confirmed pipeline of works that advances important development outcomes in Vanuatu.

Please note that this Advance Notice is not a tender process - it is simply a notification to the supply market that a procurement opportunity is forthcoming. Any tender information sent to us will not be considered at this stage.

We intend to release the Registration of Interest (ROI) in Q1 2027, with suppliers having up to 25 working days to respond, and we expect to offer a briefing session following the ROI release.

If you are interested in this opportunity, please subscribe to this GETs notice, as the RFP will be linked here once available.

item.title: CON00004041-2026 Manga-o-nua Hillcrest Library Design Services
item.description:
RFx ID: 35471034
Organisation: Hamilton City Council
Open date: Wednesday, 11 November 2026 6:00 AM +13:00
Close date: Monday, 7 December 2026 5:00 PM +13:00
Categories: 81101500 - Civil engineering
81101600 - Mechanical engineering
81101700 - Electrical and electronic engineering
95121700 - Public buildings and structures
Region: Waikato
Overview: Manga-o-nua Hillcrest Library Architectural and Multidisciplinary Design Services
Hamilton City Council is seeking proposals from suitably experienced architectural practices to provide lead architectural and multidisciplinary design services for the reinstatement and expansion of Manga-o-nua Hillcrest Library at 58 Masters Avenue, Hamilton.
The library was damaged by fire in August 2025. Before the fire, it was Council’s busiest neighbourhood library, receiving approximately 82,000 visits each year. Council intends to restore library services and develop the existing building as a contemporary, accessible, flexible and welcoming library and community facility with capacity to meet future demand.

The appointed consultant will act as lead architect, lead consultant and multidisciplinary design coordinator. The services are expected to include design-brief validation, project inception, concept design, developed design, detailed design, planning and consenting advice, building-consent documentation, stakeholder and mana whenua engagement support, cost planning, design-risk management, accessibility and fire compliance, and preparation of coordinated documentation for the future physical works procurement.
The consultant will coordinate the architectural, structural, building-services, fire, planning, landscape, cost-management and other specialist disciplines needed to deliver the project. The services will also include assessment of the existing fire-affected building and its structural elements, integration of building access and site-interface requirements, and coordination with Council’s separate transport workstream.

The procurement may include separately priced conditional portions for transport and traffic-filter design and construction-phase design support. These portions are not guaranteed and may proceed only following separate written instruction from Council.
Council will use an open, single-stage Request for Proposal and a weighted-attribute evaluation. Proposals will be assessed on methodology and delivery approach, relevant experience, key personnel and resourcing, Economic Benefit, Local Participation and price

item.title: SDC2627-1 - Kopuatama Cemetery - New Land - Concept and Construction Design - Request for Proposal - 2026
item.description:
RFx ID: 35317953
Organisation: Stratford District Council
Open date: Friday, 23 October 2026 4:00 PM +13:00
Close date: Thursday, 26 November 2026 12:00 PM +13:00
Categories: 30121800 - Landscape architecture materials
77101600 - Environmental planning
95101600 - Commercial land parcels
Region: Taranaki
Overview: Scope of Works
The project involves the preparation of concept and construction designs for the development of new land at Kopuatama Cemetery, to provide additional burial capacity and support the cemetery’s future needs.
The concept design will investigate the layout and functionality of the new area, including vehicle access between the existing and proposed cemetery areas, and the overall arrangement of burial areas and supporting infrastructure.
The objective of the project is to ensure the new land is developed in a practical, accessible, and sustainable manner that meets Council’s operational requirements and provides a respectful environment for bereaved families and visitors.

The design process will consider:
• Site constraints
• Existing cemetery operations
• Access
• Drainage
• Landscaping
• Boundary treatments
• Opportunities to enhance the visual amenity of the cemetery.

Engagement with Council representatives, iwi, and other relevant stakeholders will inform the design process to ensure cultural values, community expectations, and operational requirements are appropriately considered.
The project will progress from concept design to detailed construction design, providing the plans, specifications, and supporting information required to guide construction.

This staged approach will enable Council to:
• Assess options
• Confirm the preferred layout
• Establish project costs
• Ensure the proposed development is fit for purpose, cost-effective, and capable of meeting the cemetery’s long-term needs.
